newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai electronics seen at trillion baht by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Thai electronics seen at trillion baht by 2000.

text.p: Thai electronics production is expected to reach one trillion baht ($40 billion) by 2000, an industry source said.
Charn Asawachoke, chief executive officer of electronics giant Alphatec Group, said more than 60 percent would be for exports.
"But unless we seriously develop the industry now, we might not be able to keep or expand our market share," he told reporters.
Thailand's current world market share is around 1.3-1.4 percent. Despite sluggish trade last year, the country managed to export 300,000 million baht worth of electronics products, he said.
Charn was speaking at the ceremony to set up Thailand's first research facility for microelectronics which is partly supported by Alphatec.
"The electronics industry will be the largest and fastest growing industry in the 21st century. Many countries in the region have realised that and already set up similar centres," he said.
"We are a bit slow on that front but it is not too late to start developing the industry seriously."
Alphatec Group comprises companies that provide semiconductor-related manufacturing services, with units in Thailand, Califonia and China.
The group's only listed company in Thailand is Alphatec Electronic. (US$1 = 25 baht)
